Author: @eitansoussan8158
Comment: It s just a question of resonance frequency: each object has its own frequency at which it oscillates naturaly. You can witness it for instance by hitting the object with a little hammer, it will then oscillate back and forth at its resonance frequency. However, if you do the opposite experiment, meaning you impose an oscillation to your object , the further your imposed frequency is from the resonance frequency of the object the lower the amplitude of the oscillations will be. You can see it as "if i go too fast the system can t react but if i go too slow the system can t transmit the oscillation ".
